coronado: coronado — tonsured one, cleric (past part. used as noun; 'un coronado' is a priest with the tonsure 'crown' shaved on his head; modern coronado = 'crowned', so the sense differs; = clérigo)
jerome: Jerome — Jerónimo, the Cid's bishop of Valencia (Pidal restores Jero[me], 'don Jerome'; = Jerónimo)
llamado: llamar — called, named (past part.; so nombre es llamado 'his name is called'; = llamado)
entendido: entender — learned, knowledgeable (past part. as adjective; bien entendido es de letras 'he is well versed in letters'; = entendido)
letras: letra — letters, learning (pl.; de letras 'in book-learning'; = letras)
acordado: acordado — prudent, sensible, of sound judgment (past part. of acordar used as adjective; Pidal: 'prudente'; modern acordado = 'agreed'; = prudente, sensato)
arreziado: arreziar — vigorous, strong (past part. as adjective; mucho era arreziado 'he was very sturdy'; = arreciado, recio)
provezas: proveza — deeds of prowess, valiant deeds (pl.; = proezas)
andávalas: andar + las — he went about (them) (imperfect 3rd sg. andava + enclitic las; andávalas demandando 'he went about asking for them', i.e. seeking the Cid's feats; = las andaba demandando)
demandando: demandar — asking for, inquiring about (gerund; = demandando; modern demandar 'to sue, demand', so the sense is wider here; closest preguntando por)
sospirando: sospirar — sighing, yearning (gerund; sospirando ques viesse 'longing to find himself'; = suspirando)
viesse: veer — he might see (imperfect subjunctive 3rd sg.; ques viesse 'that he might find himself', with reflexive se; = viese)
fartás: fartar — he were to glut himself, had his fill (imperfect subjunctive 3rd sg., reduced from fartasse; sis fartás lidiando 'if he could only have his fill of fighting'; = se hartase; -ás is not a future)
sieglo: sieglo — world, secular life (Latin saeculum; a los días del sieglo 'in the days of the world', i.e. in his lifetime, ever; = siglo)
llorassen: llorar — they would weep (imperfect subjunctive 3rd pl., -assen; a los días del sieglo non le llorassen cristianos 'for as long as he lived no Christians would weep for him'; = llorasen)
gradescamos: gradescer — let us thank (present subjunctive 1st pl., jussive; nos bien gelo gradescamos 'let us give thanks for it'; = agradezcamos)
dárgelo: dar + ge + lo — to give it to him (infinitive dar + enclitic ge 'to him', ancestor of se, + lo 'it'; = darlo, dárselo)
otorgan: otorgar — they grant, agree to (present 3rd pl.; yal otorgan por obispo 'they accept him as bishop'; = otorgan)
diéronle: dar + le — they gave him (preterite 3rd pl. dieron + enclitic le; = le dieron)
rico: rico — rich, well provided (= rico; estar rico 'to be well off')
vinos: venir + se — he went away, took himself off (vino, preterite 3rd sg., + enclitic reflexive se, here spelled -s; e spidiós e vinos 'took leave and went'; = se vino, closest se fue)
remanidas: remanir — left, remaining, staying (past part. fem. pl.; tierras remanidas en paz 'lands left in peace'; no modern form, = quedadas)
dexarévos: dexar + vos — I shall leave you (split future dexaré + enclitic vos, 1st sg.; dexarévos las posadas 'I will leave you the lodgings', i.e. pass over them; = os dejaré)
demandó: demandar — he asked for, inquired after (preterite 3rd sg.; demandó por Alfonsso 'he asked for Alfonso'; = preguntó por)
fora: ser / ir — he had gone (pluperfect 3rd sg., from Latin fuerat; Pidal restores F[o]ra; fora el rey a San Fagunt 'the king had gone to Sahagún'; = había ido; modern fuera is imperfect subjunctive)
fagunt: Fagunt — Sahagún, the monastery town in León (San Fagunt = San Facundo; Fagunt apocopated; = Sahagún)
carrión: Carrión — Carrión de los Condes, town in Palencia, seat of the counts of Carrión (= Carrión)
afe: afe — behold, lo! (presentative formula, no modern form; afe Minaya 'here comes Minaya', cf. fevos; = he aquí, ahí está)
llega: llegar — he arrives (present 3rd sg.; do llega 'where he arrives'; = llega)
apuosto: apuesto — handsome, gallant, elegantly mannered (Pidal restores apu[o]sto, with diphthong; tan apuesto 'so gracefully'; = apuesto, gallardo)
puoblo: pueblo — people, assembled folk (Pidal restores pu[o]blo, with diphthong; ante tod el puoblo 'before all the people'; = pueblo)
duolo: duelo — grief, sorrow (Pidal restores du[o]lo; con grand duolo 'with great grief'; = duelo, pena; no relation to modern duelo 'duel')
besávale: besar + le — he kissed his (imperfect 3rd sg. besava + enclitic le; besávale las manos 'he kissed his hands'; = le besaba)
besávavos: besar + vos — he kisses your (imperfect 3rd sg. besava + dative vos; besávavos las manos 'he kisses your hands', a courteous greeting sent through Minaya; = os besaba, os besa)
echástesle: echar + le — you cast him out (preterite 2nd pl. echastes, = echasteis, + enclitic le; echástesle de tierra 'you banished him'; = le echasteis)
agena: ageno — foreign, another's (fem. sg.; tierra agena 'foreign land'; = ajena)
miyor: mejor — better, finest (Latin melior; spelled miyor; Murviedro que es miyor 'Murviedro, which is the better (of them)'; = mejor)
fuort: fuerte — strong (apocopated; Pidal restores fu[o]rt, with diphthong; peña fuort 'a strong rock'; = fuerte)
lides: lid — battle, combat (fem. pl.; = lides, now only 'contest, dispute'; closest batallas)
campales: campal — pitched, open-field (adjective, pl.; lides campales 'pitched battles'; = campales)
arrancó: arrancar — he routed, drove off (preterite 3rd sg.; todas las arrancó 'he routed them all', i.e. won every battle; = arrancó, derrotó)
fevos: fevos — behold, here you have (presentative formula, fe + vos 'for you'; fevos aquí las señas 'here are the tokens for you'; no modern form, = he aquí, mirad)
gruessos: gruesso — big, sturdy, heavy-built (masc. pl.; cavallos gruessos 'strong, stout horses'; = gruesos)
guarnidos: guarnir — equipped, fitted out (past part. masc. pl.; de siellas e de frenos todos guarnidos 'all fitted with saddles and bridles'; = guarnecidos)
prendades: prender — you may take, accept (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -ades; que los prendades vos 'that you accept them'; = toméis, aceptéis; modern prender 'to seize')
razonas: razonar + se — he declares himself (razona 3rd sg. present + reflexive se, reduced to -s; razonas por vuestro vassallo 'he declares himself your vassal'; = se declara)
fieras: fiero — great, mighty, extraordinary (fem. pl.; fieras ganançias 'great gains'; modern fiero 'fierce', so a weaker sense here (uncertain nuance); = grandes)
esidre: Esidre — Isidore, Saint Isidore of Seville, whose relics rest in León (Pidal restores Esidr[e]; sant Esidre; = Isidro, Isidoro)
plázme: plazer + me — it pleases me (plaze + enclitic me, accented plázme; = me place, me agrada)
plázem: plazer + me — it pleases me (plaze + me, with the pronoun written after; = me place, me agrada)
reçibo: reçebir — I receive, accept (present 1st sg.; = recibo)
garci: Garci — García (apocopated; Garci Ordóñez, count at Alfonso's court and the Cid's enemy; = García)
dexad: dexar — leave off, drop (imperative 2nd pl.; dexad essa razón 'drop that talk'; = dejad)
razón: razón — talk, speech, matter (dexad essa razón 'leave off that talk'; esta razón 'this matter'; = razón, here closest asunto, conversación)
guisas: guisa — manner, way (pl.; en todas guisas 'in every way'; = guisas, modo)
mijor: mejor — better (Latin melior, spelled mijor; mijor me sirve que vos 'he serves me better than you'; = mejor)
pide: pedir — he asks for, begs (present 3rd sg.; merçed vos pide 'he asks you for favor'; = pide)
cadiesse: caer — it should fall, should chance (imperfect subjunctive 3rd sg., Pidal restores ca[d]iesse; si vos cadiesse en sabor 'if it should fall to your liking, please you'; = cayese)
saldríen: salir — they would go out (conditional 3rd pl., old -ién ending; = saldrían)
irién: ir — they would go (conditional 3rd pl., old -ién ending; = irían)
coraçone: coraçón — heart (with an added final -e, as the poem often adds -e for the rhyme; plazme de coraçone 'it pleases me heartily'; = corazón)
mandaré: mandar — I shall order (future 1st sg.; yo les mandaré dar conducho 'I will order provisions given them'; = mandaré)
foren: ser / ir — they may go (future subjunctive 3rd pl., Pidal restores f[o]ren; mientra que por mi tierra foren 'while they go through my land'; = fueren; here the verb of motion, ir)
curiallas: curiar + las — to guard them (infinitive curiar + enclitic las, with -r assimilated before l-; de mal curiallas 'to protect them from harm'; no modern form, = guardarlas, protegerlas)
desonore: desonor — dishonor, disgrace (with an added final -e, for the rhyme; = deshonor)
catad: catar — look, see to it (imperative 2nd pl.; catad cómmo las sirvades 'see that you serve them'; = mirad; modern catar is 'to taste')
sirvades: servir — you serve, may serve (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -ades; cómmo las sirvades 'how you are to serve them'; = sirváis)
campeadore: Campeador — the Battler, the Cid's epithet (with an added final -e, for the rhyme; = Campeador)
oídme: oír + me — hear me (imperative 2nd pl. oíd + enclitic me, with -d- lost; = oídme)
pierda: perder — he lose (present subjunctive 3rd sg.; non quiero que nada pierda 'I do not want him to lose anything'; = pierda)
deseredé: desheredar — I disinherited (preterite 1st sg.; por que los deseredé 'for which I disinherited them', i.e. because of the Cid; = desheredé)
sírvanle: servir + le — let them serve him (present subjunctive 3rd pl., jussive, + enclitic le; = que le sirvan)
atrégoles: atreguar + les — I grant them a truce, protection (present 1st sg. atrego + dative les; atrégoles los cuerpos de mal 'I guarantee their persons from harm'; no modern form, = les doy tregua, les aseguro)
ocasión: ocasión — mishap, misfortune, trouble (de mal e de ocasión 'from harm and mischance'; modern ocasión 'occasion, chance', so the old sense is lost; closest daño, percance; uncertain)
sirvan: servir — they may serve (present subjunctive 3rd pl.; que sirvan a so señor 'that they serve their lord'; = sirvan)
vellido: vellido — fair, gracious, handsome (adverbial here; tan vellido fabló 'spoke so graciously'; no modern form, = bello, gentil)
servir: servir — to serve (infinitive; ir servir al Campeador 'to go serve the Campeador'; = servir)
quitos: quito — free, released (masc. pl.; de mí sean quitos 'let them be free of me', released from allegiance to the king; = libres, quitos)
desamor: desamor — ill will, disaffection (Pidal restores des[amor]; en otra desamor 'in other ill-will', Pidal's reading of a defective line; = desamor)
fabla: fabla — talk, conversation (entrar en fabla 'to enter into discussion, confer'; = habla)
casariemos: casar — we would marry (conditional 1st pl., old -iemos ending; casar con 'to marry'; = casaríamos)
acometer: acometer — to broach, venture upon, undertake (infinitive; non la osariemos acometer 'we would not dare to broach it'; = acometer, here closest emprender, plantear)
comdes: conde — counts (pl., Pidal's co[m]des; de comdes de Carrión 'of the counts of Carrión'; = condes)
espidió: espedirse — he took leave (preterite 3rd sg., with the reflexive se placed before: se espidió; = se despidió)
portero: portero — doorkeeper, usher; here a royal officer sent with the party (uncertain, Pidal's 'portero' as an escort official; = portero)
leváredes: levar — you take (future subjunctive 2nd pl., old -des ending; si leváredes las dueñas 'if you take the ladies'; = llevareis, now obsolete; closest lleváis)
sírvanlas: servir + las — let them serve them (present subjunctive 3rd pl., jussive, + enclitic las; = que las sirvan)
medina: Medina — Medinaceli, the frontier town on the Jalón where Alfonso's land ends (= Medinaceli)
denles: dar + les — let them give them (present subjunctive 3rd pl., jussive, dan + enclitic les; = que les den)
for: ser — it may be (future subjunctive 3rd sg., Pidal restores f[o]r; quanto huebos les for 'whatever they need'; = fuere)
piensse: pensar — let him take thought, look after (present subjunctive 3rd sg., jussive; piensse dellas 'let him care for them'; = piense)
vasse: ir + se — he goes away (va, present 3rd sg., + enclitic reflexive se, with doubled s; = se va)

__broaden__.señas: señas — one each, one apiece (distributive adjective, fem. pl., Latin singulas; = sendas) · also seña — banner, standard (pl.; dos señas ha cabdales 'there are two chief banners') · also seña — sign, token, proof (fevos aquí las señas 'here are the tokens (the horses) as proof'; = señas, muestras)
__broaden__.tengo: tener — I hold (present 1st sg.; en grado vos lo tengo 'I hold it to you in thanks', I am grateful; = tengo) · also tener que — 'I think that' (tengo que vos avrá pro 'I think he will be of use to you'; = creo que)
